chunks: Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام was asked about a man who needed wudu (ablution) for salat (prayer) and could not obtain water, then found water in an amount sufficient for wudu for one hundred dirhams. Is it obligatory upon him to buy it and perform wudu with it, or should he perform tayammum?
“Rather, he should buy it. Something similar happened to me, so I bought it and performed wudu, and a large amount of wealth would not grieve me because of that.”

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer) for which ritual purity is needed
key_terms.بِمِائَةِ دِرْهَمٍ: for one hundred dirhams, indicating a high purchase cost

ai.seo_question: If water for wudu is only available at a high price, should one buy it or perform tayammum?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that when water for wudu is available for purchase, even at a high price, one should buy it rather than resort to tayammum. It emphasizes the importance of taharah for salat and shows the practical example of Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام in acting upon this ruling.
